current_input_supply_summary.summary: The current path can produce attachment status, receipt, eligibility state, and agent handoff from completed-run status. It cannot produce a useful run-specific brief, enriched brief, or triage read without safe supplied artifacts or a future resolver.

required_inputs.safe_default_policy: Use only for structured artifact presence, parseability, relative run refs, and blocker state.
required_inputs.notes: The runtime hook already passes the completed run directory to the bundle path.

required_inputs.safe_default_policy: Use repo default contract refs and reject unsupported schema versions.
required_inputs.notes: These contracts govern the bundle but do not supply semantic brief content.

required_inputs.current_source: populated brief artifact, if one already exists
required_inputs.safe_default_policy: Do not synthesize from raw conversation in runtime; defer until a bounded interpreter or resolver-approved artifact exists.
required_inputs.notes: The packet builder can prepare metadata, but it explicitly does not fill the brief.

required_inputs.safe_default_policy: Copy only resolver-approved safe refs; otherwise record deferred_missing_brief.
required_inputs.notes: Existing checked-in examples are safe for known cases, not a general runtime supply path.

required_inputs.safe_default_policy: Copy only when rendered brief and interpretation read are resolver-approved; otherwise defer enrichment.
required_inputs.notes: The enrichment builder is deterministic, but it depends on an existing interpretation read.

required_inputs.safe_default_policy: Keep out of runtime generation; route to offline or calibrated interpretation before enrichment.
required_inputs.notes: Existing reads support checked-in examples; arbitrary live runs need a future interpretation process.

required_inputs.safe_default_policy: Allow metadata-only packet generation in a future resolver, but never treat the packet as a triage read.
required_inputs.notes: The current triage packet builder is focused on the three checked-in-safe examples rather than arbitrary runtime runs.

required_inputs.current_source: existing provisional triage read, if available
required_inputs.safe_default_policy: Defer user-surface routing unless a resolver-approved triage read exists.
required_inputs.notes: Triage reads route attention; they must not become scores or approval labels.

required_inputs.safe_default_policy: Generate deterministically from run artifact status, supplied refs, blockers, and deferred reasons.
required_inputs.notes: This is the core safe artifact the runtime hook can always try to write when flagged.

required_inputs.safe_default_policy: Compute only from artifact presence, parseability, path safety, custody flags, and explicit triage routes.
required_inputs.notes: The gate must not infer messy semantic meaning.

required_inputs.safe_default_policy: Render from attachment status and never render the full brief by default.
required_inputs.notes: Receipt quality improves only when a safe action-consequence or brief ref exists.

required_inputs.safe_default_policy: Generate from status, refs, missingness, and explicit route outputs; keep action authorization false.
required_inputs.notes: Useful for inspection, but sparse when runtime supply is deferred.

required_inputs.current_source: completed run artifacts and supplied safe refs
required_inputs.safe_default_policy: Carry relative refs and source status only; do not copy raw/private content.
required_inputs.notes: Source refs are necessary but not sufficient for a user-useful brief.

unsafe_auto_supply_inputs.reason: Contains private conversation context and must not be default-exported into sidecars, receipts, or agent handoffs.
May contain sensitive user-facing answer content; runtime supply should preserve refs/status by default.
Memo prose can contain private context and should not become default sidecar material.
Provider artifacts are not safe default handoff content.
Private ledgers can inform local review but must not be copied into runtime sidecars by default.
Agent-facing and checked-in-safe outputs must use relative refs or status, not local machine paths.
Local-private packet mode can include sensitive text and must remain operator-only unless explicitly reviewed.
Creating interpretation inside the runtime attachment path would add model/provider calls and overtrust risk.

options_considered.finding: Safest current mode and already supported by PR162, but too manual and not generally run-specific.
Useful for demos and regression tests, but not enough for arbitrary live runs and easy to overread as product completeness.
Useful as part of the next contract for run-specific metadata and deferred statuses, but it cannot fill semantic brief fields alone.
Needed for future semantic interpretation, but it should be connected through a supply resolver contract rather than ad hoc runtime behavior.
Valuable for internal review but unsafe as the default runtime or agent handoff supply path.
Rejected for now because it would add provider/model calls and make runtime attachment responsible for messy semantic interpretation.
Best next step: define supply modes, resolver output statuses, safe refs, deferred reasons, and queue handoff before implementation.

recommended_next_pr: PR170 Decision Work Brief Runtime Safe Supply Resolver Contract v0
strongest_useful_signal: The runtime-attached path already has enough deterministic machinery to preserve status, blockers, receipts, and handoff refs safely; the next work can focus on supplying semantic inputs rather than more hook plumbing.
strongest_unresolved_risk: For arbitrary live runs, useful brief/enriched/triage inputs still require bounded interpretation or resolver-approved safe artifacts. Without that, the runtime hook remains correctly deferred.
overclaim_risk: A resolver or registry could make curated examples look like general product readiness. PR170 must keep registry, local-private, queue, and runtime paths visibly separate.
